claims: 從來沒…過 is a natural Mandarin pattern for emphatic experiential negation.
沒 negates experiential 過 while 過 remains; the construction does not merely encode simple past.

sources.citation: Ross, C., & Ma, J.-h. S. Modern Mandarin Chinese Grammar: A Practical Guide. Section 17.3, experiential aspect.
Chinese Grammar Wiki (AllSet Learning). Expressing “never” with 從來.

claims: 曾經 is a past-time adverb and commonly combines with V過 for prior experience.
過 contributes experiential aspect; the construction does not require a specific past time.

sources.citation: Ross, C., & Ma, J.-h. S. Modern Mandarin Chinese Grammar: A Practical Guide. Section 17.3, experiential aspect.
Merry Mandarin Grammar Lab. 曾經 (céngjīng): past/once; action verbs commonly pair with 過.

entry.notes: R44 audit: explanation and examples are accurate; wording appropriately distinguishes 曾經 from 過.

claims: 有 + V is a documented and salient Taiwan Mandarin construction.
Taiwan Mandarin usage includes 有 + V過 patterns such as 我有去過那個地方.
The entry correctly presents 有V過 as a regional pattern rather than the only acceptable experiential form.

sources.citation: Yang, Y.-X. (2019). The Syntactic and Pragmatic Characteristics of the Construction “you zai V” in Taiwan Mandarin. National Taiwan University. DOI 10.6342/NTU201900465.
Learn Teochew. Grammatical Differences in Taiwanese Mandarin: 有 + V, including 我有去過那個地方.

entry.notes: R44 audit: Taiwan-specific framing is supported. Examples are acceptable colloquial Taiwan Mandarin; no correction required.

claims: 沒 + V + 過 is the standard negation of experiential 過.
The distinction between 沒V過 (absence of prior experience) and a simple negated past event is correctly explained.

sources.citation: Ross, C., & Ma, J.-h. S. Modern Mandarin Chinese Grammar: A Practical Guide. Section 17.3, experiential aspect.

claims: Verb + 過 marks experiential aspect: an event has occurred at least once before without requiring a specified time.
過 is not a past-tense ending and contrasts with 了 in aspectual function.

sources.citation: Ross, C., & Ma, J.-h. S. Modern Mandarin Chinese Grammar: A Practical Guide. Section 17.3, experiential aspect.

entry.notes: R44 audit: core explanation and examples are accurate. The 了/過 contrast is simplified but pedagogically appropriate at A2.
